en: When the hina dolls appear in the box, how could one forget to put on a solemn expression? -- Buson
u.src: 当雏人偶出现在箱子里的时候，怎忘记摆出严肃的面容？——芜村

en: This is the story of an old woman.
u.src: 这是一个老妇人的故事。

en: I had arranged with an American living in Yokohama to sell him the hina dolls in November.
u.src: 我和住在横滨的美国人约定，在十一月的时候会把雏人偶卖给他。

en: Our family shop was called Kinokuniya, and for generations my forebears had run a money-changing business, mainly raising funds for various feudal lords.
u.src: 我家店铺的名字叫做纪之国屋，父辈们几代都开钱庄的，钱庄主要是为各路诸侯筹措资金。

en: My grandfather in particular, who used the art name Shichiku, was a man of very refined and elegant tastes, and the set of hina dolls he left me was also exquisitely delicate and finely made.
u.src: 尤其是我的祖父，祖父号为紫竹，是一个十分有情趣的风雅之士，他给我留下来的那套雏人偶也是十分精巧细致。

en: For example, in the palace arranged on the top tier, the crown on the empress doll's head was decorated with coral-inlaid pendants,
u.src: 以此为例，摆放在最高层皇居内，皇后人偶头上的皇冠是以珊瑚镶嵌的璎珞做装饰，

en: and the sash worn by the emperor doll was made of silk, with outer and inner patterns embroidered on it alternately,
u.src: 天皇人偶佩戴腰带是丝绸质地，上面交替绣着表纹和里纹，

en: that was how refined and carefully crafted this set of hina dolls was.
u.src: 这套雏人偶就是这么的精致考究。

en: However, by the time it passed to my father, the twelfth-generation Kinokuniya Ihei,
u.src: 可是，传到我父亲——第十二代纪之国屋伊兵卫的时候，

en: he had no choice but to sell this set of hina dolls, which shows how far our family had fallen by then.
u.src: 他不得不变卖这套雏人偶，可以想象当时我家落魄到了什么地步。

en: In any case, after the Tokugawa shogunate collapsed, only the Kaga domain reduced its taxes.
u.src: 不管怎么样，德川幕府政权瓦解之后，也就只有加贺藩降低了赋税。

en: Even so, it merely reduced the levy of three thousand ryo by one hundred ryo.
u.src: 不过，也只是从三千两的税赋里减少一百两罢了。

en: After that, the family also suffered two or three fires.
u.src: 这之后，家里有遇上了两三次祝融灾祸。

en: Even the umbrella business was no longer doing nearly as well as before,
u.src: 就连经营蝙蝠伞的营生也大不如前了，

en: so, in order to keep the family fed and clothed, they could only gradually sell off some of their better household possessions.
u.src: 因此为了解决家里人的温饱问题，只能慢慢变卖一些像样的家当了。

en: Around this time, an antique dealer called Marusa urged my father to sell the hina dolls.
u.src: 这个时候，有一家名叫丸佐的古董商劝说父亲卖掉雏人偶。

en: By now, however, the owner of that shop has also passed away; he was a rather comical-looking man with a slightly bald head.
u.src: 不过，如今这家的老板也已经去世了，那是一个头有点秃、样子极为滑稽的人。

en: In the middle of the top of his head he had a tattoo, as if a smelly dogskin plaster had been stuck there.
u.src: 他脑袋顶中间有一块刺青，就像贴着一快臭臭的狗皮膏药一样。

en: According to the owner himself, when he was young he had it done to hide the slight bald spot on top of his head,
u.src: 听老板自己说，这是他年轻的时候为了遮掩微秃的头顶，

en: having specially asked someone to tattoo it there, only never expecting that later the whole back of his head would go completely bald,
u.src: 专门请人刺上去的，只是没想到后来自己的整个后脑门都秃光了，

ja: ってしまったのである。
en: leaving only this tattoo on his forehead.
u.src: 只剩下了脑门上这块刺青。

en: At that time I was only fifteen, and although the owner of Marusa urged him several times, my father refused in the end to sell the hina dolls.
u.src: 那个时候，我只有十五岁，尽管丸佐老板数次劝说，父亲最后都拒绝卖掉雏人偶。

en: In the end, it was my elder brother who had no choice but to sell them...
u.src: 最终，还是我的哥哥被逼无奈才卖掉的……

en: He too is no longer among the living now.
u.src: 同样，他现在也不在人世了。

en: At that time, my brother was still an impulsive, proud eighteen-year-old boy.
u.src: 那时候，哥哥还是个容易冲动的好强的十八岁男孩。

en: My brother could probably be considered an enlightened modern man.
u.src: 哥哥应该算是一个文明开化的人。

en: He often read English readers and was passionate about politics.
u.src: 他经常看英文读本，热衷政治。

en: Whenever someone brought up the hina dolls,
u.src: 只要有人提起雏人偶，

en: he would say contemptuously that things like the Girls' Festival were nothing but outdated bad customs,
u.src: 他就轻蔑地说女儿节之类的不过是陈旧陋习，

en: and ask what use there was in displaying things with no practical purpose.
u.src: 摆那种没什么实际用处的东西又有什么用呢？

en: Over this matter, my brother argued many times with our tradition-respecting mother.
u.src: 为了这件事，哥哥和尊重传统的母亲争执了很多次。

en: But if we sold the hina dolls,
u.src: 但是只要卖了雏人偶，

en: at least the whole family could get safely through the end of the year,
u.src: 至少可以让全家安然度过年关，

en: so he did not insist on his own opinion in front of our father, who was frantic over raising money.
u.src: 因此也没有在为了筹钱而焦头烂额的父亲面前坚持自己的想法。
正想前面所说的，

en: it had already been decided that the hina dolls would be sold in November to an American living in Yokohama.
u.src: 雏人偶已经决定在十一月卖给在横滨住的美国人了。
你问我吗？

en: Are you asking what I thought at the time?
u.src: 你问我当时有什么想法？

en: Although I naturally had some complaints,
u.src: 虽然难免有些抱怨，

en: I was, after all, an easygoing sort of girl to begin with,
u.src: 不过我原本就是个大大咧咧的女孩子，

en: and besides, Father promised me that after the hina dolls were sold,
u.src: 况且父亲答应我雏人偶卖掉之后

en: he would buy me a purple silk sash.
u.src: 要买一条紫色绸缎腰带送给我。

en: On the second evening after this matter had been settled, the owner of Marusa came back from Yokohama and made a special visit to my house.
u.src: 这件事说好之后的第二个晚上，丸佐老板从横滨回来了，专门来我家拜访。

ja: されることはなかった。
en: After our house suffered its third fire, it was never rebuilt.
u.src: 我家在遭遇第三次火灾之后，就没有重新修建。

en: The whole family lived in the storehouse that had escaped the great fire, and we added a shop onto the outside.
u.src: 全家人都住在没被大火烧毁的仓库里，并且往外面搭建出一个店铺来。

en: Since it was a hastily opened pharmacy to begin with, all it had was a metal signboard with names of medicines such as Shotokugan, Chokeigan, and Ketai-dokusan written on it, along with a medicine cabinet.
u.src: 本来就是仓促开的药铺，所以只有一个金属招牌，上面写着正德丸、调经丸、去胎毒散等药名，以及一座药柜。

en: Oh yes, there was also an endless lamp.
u.src: 对了，还有一盏无尽灯。

en: You may not know what kind of lamp that was.
u.src: 可能大家不知道这是什么灯。

en: In fact, it was nothing more than an old-fashioned oil lamp that used rapeseed oil instead of kerosene.
u.src: 其实不过是一种用油菜籽代替煤油的老式油灯。

en: Strangely enough, even now, whenever I smell medicinal ingredients like dried tangerine peel or rhubarb, I cannot help thinking of that endless lamp.
u.src: 说起来很有意思，到如今，我只要闻到诸如陈皮、大黄等药材的气味，就会不由自主的想起无尽灯。

en: Yes, that evening, the endless lamp bathed the whole room in dim light, and the smell of medicinal herbs still drifted through the room.
u.src: 没错，那天晚上，无尽灯将整个屋子笼罩在昏暗的灯光下，屋里还飘散着药材的气味。

en: The bald owner of Marusa and my father, who had cut off his topknot, sat facing each other with the mujinto lamp between them.
u.src: 秃头的丸佐老板和剪掉了发髻的父亲，隔着无尽灯，对面而坐

en: This is half of the full amount. Please confirm receipt.
u.src: “我是全款的一半金额，请你查收。”

en: After they had exchanged polite greetings, the owner took out the money wrapped in paper.
u.src: 彼此客气寒暄一番后，老板取出包在纸里的钱。

en: It was probably arranged that he would pay the deposit that day.
u.src: 可能是定好了那天付定金吧。

en: Father warmed his hands over the brazier and quietly bowed to show his thanks.
u.src: 父亲将手放在火炉上面取暖，静静的鞠了一躬以示谢意。

en: At that point, Mother told me to carry in the tea.
u.src: 这时，母亲安排我端茶进去。

ja: に「いけない、いけない、これはいけない」と
en: As I was serving the tea, the owner of Marusa suddenly said loudly, "No, no, this will not do."
u.src: 正在我奉茶的时候，丸佐老板突然高声说：“不行，不行，这不行。”

en: I thought he meant there was something wrong with the way I served the tea and stood there dumbfounded, but in fact there was another packet of money in front of the owner.
u.src: 我以为是说我奉茶不行，怔怔的杵在一旁，原来是老板面前有另一包钱。

en: It is not much, just a small token of my appreciation.
u.src: “钱不多，一点心意。”

en: Oh, please don't laugh at me!
u.src: “哎呀！请别笑话我啦！”

en: Please do not tease me like that.
u.src: “你就别跟我开玩笑啦。

en: When you do that, sir, I am the one who feels embarrassed!
u.src: 老爷这么做我才觉得尴尬呢！

en: We are not strangers, after all.
u.src: 我们也不是外人。

en: Since the old master's generation, Marusa has received such great kindness from your family!
u.src: 从老太爷那一代开始，丸佐就备受您家族的照顾呢！

en: Please do not stand on ceremony like that; do stay here yourself.
u.src: 您千万别这么见外，还请您自己留下来吧。
呀，小姐。
你好！

en: The butterfly-style coiffure you are wearing today is very beautiful!
u.src: 你今天梳的蝴蝶发髻，十分美丽呢！”

en: I listened absentmindedly to their conversation, then went back to the storehouse.
u.src: 我心不在焉的听着他们这些对话，就回仓库去了。

en: The storehouse was about the size of twelve tatami mats.
u.src: 仓库大概有十二张榻榻米那么大。

en: It had once been fairly spacious, but now that it held wardrobes, a long brazier, storage cabinets, shelves, and many other pieces of furniture, it felt somewhat cramped.
u.src: 本来还算宽敞，但如今放了衣柜、长形火炉、收纳柜、置物架等诸多家具，就显得有些狭小了。

en: Among all these household things, the most conspicuous were more than thirty paulownia boxes.
u.src: 这所有的家当里边，最突出的就是三十几个桐木箱子。

ja: がつかなかっただろう
en: If I did not tell you why, you probably would never guess.
u.src: 倘若我不说是为什么，你估计也猜不到。

en: What was packed inside the boxes was a set of hina dolls.
u.src: 箱子里装着的就是雏人偶。

en: So that they could be carried away at any time, they had been kept piled near the wall by the window.
u.src: 为了方便随时搬走，因此一直堆在靠窗的墙壁附近。

en: Because the oil lamp had been taken to be used in the shop, only a dim paper lantern was lit in the storehouse.
u.src: 因为无尽灯被拿去店里使用，所以仓库里只点着朦胧的纸灯笼。

en: In the dim light, Mother was sewing medicine pouches, and my elder brother sat at an old, small desk reading an English book.
u.src: 在朦胧的灯光下，母亲正在缝制药袋，哥哥坐在又旧又小的书桌前读英文书。

en: Everything was just as it usually was.
u.src: 一切和平常没什么两样。

en: But when I happened to glance at Mother, though her hands were still doing needlework, tears had already filled the lashes of her lowered eyelids.
u.src: 不过，我不经意间看了母亲一眼，母亲的手上虽然做着针线活，但是低垂眼睑的睫毛里面已经盈满泪水。

en: I returned after serving the tea, full of hope that Mother would praise me.
u.src: 我奉茶回来，满心期待得到母亲的夸奖，

en: That may be putting it a little too strongly, but I really did have that expectation.
u.src: 可能这么说有点夸张，不过的确是有这种期待的。

en: Perhaps it would be more accurate to say that seeing Mother's tears made me feel sad, or rather left me at a loss.
u.src: 可能说因为看到了母亲的泪水，我有些悲伤，或者说不知所措更为准确。

en: To escape Mother's tears, I sat down beside my elder brother.
u.src: 为了躲开母亲的泪水，我坐在了哥哥身边。

en: At that moment, my brother Eikichi suddenly raised his head and looked at Mother in surprise,
u.src: 这个时候，哥哥英吉突然抬起头来，惊讶的看了看母亲，

en: then looked at me, smiled in a strange way, and went on reading his English book.
u.src: 又看了看我，诡异的笑了笑，然后接着读他的英文书。

en: Never had I hated my brother, who called himself civilized and enlightened, as much as I did then.
u.src: 我从没有像那个时候一样，痛恨我这个自称文明开化的哥哥。

en: He looks down on Mother in his heart, I thought to myself.
u.src: 他心里瞧不起母亲，我心里这么想着。

en: I suddenly struck my brother hard on the back.
u.src: 我猛然用力锤向哥哥的背部。
“你干什么啊？”

en: My older brother glared fiercely at me.
u.src: 哥哥凶狠的瞪着我。

en: I'm going to hit you, I'm going to hit you...
u.src: “我要打你，我要打你……”

en: I could not help crying as I hit my brother.
u.src: 我不由的一边哭，一边打着哥哥。

en: At that moment, I had completely forgotten that my brother was a hot-tempered man.
u.src: 当时，我全然忘了哥哥是个脾气暴躁的人。

en: Just before my hand was about to land on my brother, he slapped me across the face.
u.src: 就在我的手刚要落到哥哥身上之前，哥哥打了我一个耳光。
“不懂事的小妮子。”

en: I immediately burst into loud sobs.
u.src: 我立马放声大哭。

en: At the same time, a ruler came down on my older brother.
u.src: 同时，一把尺落在哥哥身上。

en: My older brother immediately protested vehemently, and my mother, too, argued with him in a trembling whisper.
u.src: 哥哥立马激烈抗议，母亲也颤抖着声音低声跟他理论。

en: During this quarrel, I kept crying bitterly in frustration.
u.src: 在这场争吵当中，我始终懊恼的痛哭流涕。

en: When Father had seen off the owner of Marusa and came back from the shop to the storehouse carrying the Mujinto lamp,
u.src: 等到父亲送走丸佐的老板，拿着无尽灯从店里回到仓库的时候，

en: No, not only I, but even my brother suddenly fell silent when he saw Father's expression.
u.src: 不，不仅仅是我，就连哥哥也在看到父亲的神色后，突然闭嘴不言。

en: To me, my silent father was far more frightening than my brother had been in his fierceness then.
u.src: 对我来说，沉默的父亲比当时凶狠的哥哥更加的可怕。

en: That evening, everything had been settled,
u.src: 当晚，所有的事情都谈好了，

en: when the other half of the payment was received at the end of the month,
u.src: 等到月底收下另一半金额的时候，

en: the hina dolls were to be handed over to an American living in Yokohama.
u.src: 就要将雏人偶交给住在横滨的美国人。

en: What? You ask how much they sold for altogether?
u.src: 什么？你问总共卖了多少钱？

en: Looking back now, it seems truly unbelievable, but it was only thirty yen.
u.src: 现在想来，真觉得难以置信，真的只有三十圆。

en: Still, by the prices of the time, that was a fairly good price.
u.src: 不过，以当时的物价，这个价钱还算是不错的。

en: Before long, the day when the hina dolls would be sent away drew closer and closer.
u.src: 很快，距离送走雏人偶的日子越来越近。

en: As I said before, I did not feel especially sad about selling the hina dolls.
u.src: 就像我前面讲述的，我对于卖掉雏人偶这件事并没有感到特别的悲伤。

en: But as the day to send them away came nearer day by day, I unconsciously began to feel the sadness of parting from the hina dolls.
u.src: 但是，随着要送走雏人偶的日子一天比一天逼近，我在不知不觉中开始感到了即将和雏人偶分别的悲伤。

en: Although I was still a child then, I was not so selfish as to want to keep at home the hina dolls that had already been promised for sale to someone else.
u.src: 虽然我当时还是个孩子，但是我也不会任性的想要把已经说好要卖给别人的雏人偶留在家里。

en: I only wanted to look at them once more before handing the hina dolls over.
u.src: 我只是想在把雏人偶交出去之前，能够再看看它们——

en: The emperor and empress inside the yellow palace, the five musicians, the cherry tree on the left, the orange tree on the right, the paper lanterns, the folding screen, and the maki-e furnishings.
u.src: 黄居内的天皇、皇后，五人组的乐团，左边的樱花树，右边的橘子树，纸灯笼，屏风，莳绘道具。

en: I wanted to set them out in the storehouse and look at them one more time.
u.src: 我想把它们摆在仓库里，再看一次。

en: But no matter how earnestly I begged, my stubborn father absolutely refused.
u.src: 但是不管我怎么恳请，性格固执的父亲死活都不答应。

en: Once we have accepted the deposit, no matter where they are displayed, they belong to someone else.
u.src: “只要手下定金，不管摆在哪里，那都是别人家的东西了。”

en: That was what my father said.
u.src: 父亲这么说。

en: It was the end of the month, on a day when a strong wind was blowing.
u.src: 月底，一个刮大风的日子。

en: My mother, perhaps because she had caught a cold or because a boil the size of a grain had formed on her mouth, said she did not feel well and had no appetite even for breakfast.
u.src: 母亲不知道是因为感冒，还是嘴上长了一颗足有谷粒大小的肿疮的缘故，说自己身体不太舒服，早饭都没胃口吃。

en: After my mother and I finished tidying the kitchen together, she rested one hand on her forehead and looked down at the brazier with her head lowered.
u.src: 我和母亲一起收拾完厨房之后，母亲一只手放在额头上，低垂着头看着火炉。

en: Before long, when noon came, she suddenly raised her head.
u.src: 很快，到了正午时候，她忽然抬起头来。

en: I saw that the boil on my mother's mouth was as red as a tomato.
u.src: 我看到母亲嘴上的肿疮红的像番茄。

en: Then, seeing an unusual light flashing in her eyes, I knew she had a high fever.
u.src: 再看她眼睛迸发出不同寻常的光辉，就知道她是在发高烧。

en: Once I recognized the fire of that reality, I was startled, threw everything else aside, and rushed straight out to find my father.
u.src: 认清这个现实之火，我吓了一跳，什么也不管不顾了，直接冲出去找到爸爸。

en: Dad, Dad, Mom is very seriously ill!
u.src: “爸爸，爸爸，妈妈病的很严重！”

en: Father and my elder brother, who was there, came in together.
u.src: 父亲以及在场的哥哥，一起走了进来。

en: Perhaps they had been frightened by Mother's terrible expression.
u.src: 也许是被母亲可怕的脸惊吓到了吧！

en: Even Father, who was usually quiet and cautious, looked blank and did not know what to do.
u.src: 平时一向低调谨慎的父亲也一脸茫然，不知所措。

ja: したことじゃありません。
en: Mother, however, forced out a smile and said, "Oh, it is nothing serious.
u.src: 母亲却勉强的挤出微笑，说：“哎呦，不是什么大不了的事儿。

en: I only scratched myself by accident with a fingernail.
u.src: 只是不小心被指甲划破了罢了。

en: I still have to hurry and make lunch."
u.src: 我还要抓紧去做午饭。”
“别勉强。
让阿鹤做午饭就行了。”

en: Father cut Mother off, half scolding her,
u.src: 父亲半训斥的打断母亲的话，

en: Eikichi, hurry and bring Doctor Honma to the house.
u.src: “英吉，快点去请本间大夫来家里。”

en: After hearing that, his elder brother ran out of the shop like a gust of wind.
u.src: 哥哥听到之后，如一阵风般跑出店外。

en: Doctor Honma was a practitioner of Chinese medicine.
u.src: 本间大夫是一位中医。

en: But my elder brother thought he was a quack and looked down on him deeply.
u.src: 不过哥哥觉得他是个庸医，很是瞧不起他。

en: When he examined Mother, my brother always stood to one side with his arms crossed, watching with suspicion.
u.src: 在他帮母亲看病的时候，哥哥始终双臂交叉站在一旁，用怀疑的眼光旁观。

en: Honma said that what had appeared on Mother's face was facial sores.
u.src: 本间说母亲脸上长的是面疮。

en: In fact, this illness called facial sores was not originally anything malignant; it could be cured simply by cutting them away in an operation.
u.src: 其实面疮这个病原本不是什么恶疾，动手术切掉就好了。

en: But the sad thing was that at the time surgery was simply impossible.
u.src: 但是可悲的是当时根本做不了手术。

en: All they could do was decoct medicine for her to drink and buy leeches to draw blood from the wound.
u.src: 只能煎药服用，买水蛭吸掉伤口上的血。

en: Father stayed by Mother's bedside day after day, decocting medicine according to Doctor Honma's prescription.
u.src: 父亲日日守在母亲床边，按照本间大夫的药方煎药。

en: Every day my brother took fifteen sen and went out to buy leeches.
u.src: 哥哥每天取十五钱到外面买水蛭。

en: Even I... I too slipped away without my brother knowing and ran to the Inari shrine nearest our house to pray for Mother.
u.src: 就连我……我也瞒着哥哥，跑到离家最近的稻荷神社为母亲祈福。

en: Because of this, no one in the family had any time to concern themselves with the hina dolls.
u.src: ——因为这件事，全家人都无暇顾忌雏人偶。

en: No, to be more precise, no one in the family even felt like glancing at the thirty-odd paulownia boxes piled against the wall.
u.src: 不，准确的说，全家人连看一眼堆在墙边的三十几个桐木箱子的心情都没有。

en: However, on November twenty ninth, the day before I had to part with the hina dolls,
u.src: 然而，到了和雏人偶分离的前一天，十一月二十九，

en: I realized that this would be the last day I could spend with them,
u.src: 我想到这将是我和雏人偶在一起的最后一天，

en: and I truly could not help wanting to open the box and look at the hina dolls one more time.
u.src: 真的忍不住想要打开箱子再看雏人偶一眼。

en: But in my heart I knew that no matter how earnestly I begged my father, he would never agree.
u.src: 但是，我心里明白，不管我怎么央求父亲，他都不会答应的。

en: Yes, I would beg my mother to plead for me, though that idea came to me at once,
u.src: 嗯，恳请母亲替我求情！——虽然我心里马上想到这个办法 ，

en: but my mother's illness was growing worse and worse, and aside from a little rice gruel, she could not eat anything.
u.src: 但是母亲的病越来越重了，除了一点米汤之外，什么都吃不下去。

en: Especially over these last few days, pus streaked with blood kept flowing into her mouth.
u.src: 尤其是这几天，带着血丝的脓不停的流进她的嘴里。

en: Seeing my mother in that state, even the most thoughtless fifteen year old girl would not have had the nerve to ask that the hina dolls be set out.
u.src: 看到母亲这幅情形，即使再不懂事的十五岁女孩，也没胆量提出把雏人偶摆出来的事。

en: From early in the morning I stayed by my mother's bedside, carefully watching her color and her mood,
u.src: 我一大早就开始守在母亲床边，仔细看母亲的神色和心情，

en: and until afternoon snack time, I still could not bring myself to say what I was thinking.
u.src: 一直到下午的点心时间，我都没能把自己的想法说出口。

en: But below the wire-mesh window in front of me, paulownia boxes holding hina dolls were piled up.
u.src: 但是，我面前的铁丝网窗口下面，就堆放着装着雏人偶的桐木箱子。

en: After tonight, these boxes would be sent to the homes of foreigners living in Yokohama, and perhaps even cross the ocean to America.
u.src: 过了今晚，这些箱子就会被送到住在横滨的外国人家里……搞不好还会远渡重洋到美国。

en: The more I thought about it, the more unbearable it felt.
u.src: 我越想越觉得无法忍受。

en: When my mother had fallen fast asleep, I quietly ran to the shop.
u.src: 等母亲熟睡的时候，我悄悄跑到店里。

en: Although the sunlight did not reach the shop very well.
u.src: 虽然店里的阳光照射不太好。

en: Still, compared with the storeroom, I could at least see people passing along the road, so it was much brighter.
u.src: 但是比起仓库来，至少可以看到路上的行人，明朗的多。

en: At that time, Father was checking the accounts, and my elder brother was carefully putting licorice root and other medicines into the mortar.
u.src: 那个时候，父亲正在核对账目，哥哥正在认真的将甘草之类的药物放进药碾。

en: Dad, that is my greatest wish...
u.src: “爸爸，那是我最大的心愿……”

en: Watching my father's expression, I told him what I was thinking.
u.src: 我看着父亲的脸色，说出了自己的想法。

en: But my father not only refused; he could not even be bothered to pay any attention to me.
u.src: 但是父亲不仅不答应，甚至理都懒得理我。

en: I already told you about this last time.
u.src: “这个事情我上次已经说过了。

en: Oh, Eikichi, go over to Marusa once today before it gets dark.
u.src: 对了，英吉，今天你天黑之前，去一趟丸佐。”

en: Are you going to Marusa to see the owner?
u.src: “去丸佐，找老板吗？”

en: Just ask him to buy an oil lamp, and bring it back with you while you are at it.
u.src: “就是麻烦他帮忙买一盏油灯……你顺便拿回来。”

en: But Marusa does not sell oil lamps, does it?
u.src: “但是丸佐没有卖油灯啊？”

en: Father paid no attention to me at all, but gave a rare smile and said:
u.src: 父亲根本理都没理我，难得的笑了笑说：

en: It is not as though I am buying a candlestick or anything like that; I only want to ask him to help buy an oil lamp...
u.src: “也不是买烛台之类的东西，只是请他帮忙买一盏油灯……

en: If he handles the purchase, it should turn out better than if I bought it myself.
u.src: 由他出面买的话，应该会我买的还好吧。”

ja: わなくなったのですか。」
en: So, after that, did they stop using the Mujinto lamp at home?
u.src: “那么，之后家里不用无尽灯了吗？”

en: When business is bad, they will probably still use it.
u.src: “生意不好的时候，还会用吧。”

en: Yes, old things should be discarded one by one.
u.src: “是啊，古老的东西就应该一件一件淘汰掉。

en: In any case, if we light the oil lamp, Mother will feel much brighter too, won't she?
u.src: 无论如何，点上油灯的话，妈妈的心情也会明朗很多吧。”

en: After Father finished speaking, he lowered his head again and went on fiddling with the abacus.
u.src: 父亲说完，又低垂头继续摆弄算盘。

en: Other people ignoring my wish only made my desire to see it fulfilled grow more urgent.
u.src: 别人不理会我愿望，却让我想要实现的愿望的心情更加迫切。

en: I shook Father by the shoulder from behind once more.
u.src: 我再次从后面摇了摇父亲的肩膀。
“爸爸，行不行嘛？”
“别再啰嗦了。”

en: Without even turning his head, Father suddenly scolded me.
u.src: 父亲头也没回，突然骂了我一句。

ja: それだけでなく、そばの
en: Not only that, even my elder brother beside him gave me a malicious glare.
u.src: 不仅这样，就连旁边的哥哥也不怀好意的瞪了我一眼。

en: Dejected, I quietly went back into the room.
u.src: 我垂头丧气的悄悄回到屋里。

en: At some point, Mother had opened her eyes and awakened, and was looking at the hand she had laid across her face.
u.src: 不知何时，母亲已经睁开眼醒了过来，看着自己搭在脸上的手掌。

en: When she saw me come into the room, she asked with surprising clarity, "Did your father scold you?"
u.src: 看到我走进屋里，竟然无比清醒的 问：“你爸爸是不是骂你了？”

en: I did not know what to say, and just kept fiddling with the key beside the bed.
u.src: 我不知道怎么说，直摆弄床边的钥匙。

ja: ってはいけないことを
en: You said something you shouldn't have again, didn't you?
u.src: “你又说了什么不该说的话吧？”

en: Mother looked at me and said with great difficulty:
u.src: 母亲看着我，很为难的说：

en: “I am not well now, and the whole family depends on your father alone to look after us, so you must be obedient.
u.src: “现在我身体不好，全家都靠你爸爸一个人照顾，你要听话。

en: The daughter next door often goes to see plays, so you should go along with her too...”
u.src: 隔壁家的女儿经常去看戏，你也跟着一起……”

en: I do not want to go see a play.
u.src: “我不想去看戏。”

en: It is not just watching the play; there are lots of things you like to look at too, such as hairstyles and haneri collars.
u.src: “也不只是看戏，诸如发髻、半襟，有很多你喜欢的东西都可以看看啊。”

en: Hearing those words from my mother, I could not tell whether I felt regret or sadness, and before I knew it I began to cry.
u.src: 听到母亲这些话，我不知道是后悔还是难过，不由哭了起来。

en: Mama, I... I don't want anything... I only want, before the hina dolls are put away...
u.src: “妈妈，我…………什么也不想要……我只想在雏人偶送走之前……”
“雏人偶？

en: Before sending the Hina dolls away?
u.src: 雏人偶送走之前？”

en: Mother's eyes opened even wider, and she stared intently at me.
u.src: 母亲眼睛睁得更大了，凝视着我。

en: Suddenly, I found myself a little unable to speak.
u.src: 突然，我有点说不出口了。

en: Halfway through speaking, I suddenly realized that my older brother Eikichi had somehow come to stand behind me.
u.src: 话说了一半，猛然发现哥哥英吉不知何时站在我身后了。

en: My brother wore a look of contempt for me and said coldly, "You foolish little girl!
u.src: 哥哥露出瞧不起我的表情，冷漠的说：“你这不懂事的小妮子！

en: What difference do the hina dolls make?
u.src: 雏人偶又能如何？

en: Have you forgotten how Father scolded you just now?"
u.src: 你忘了刚才爸爸怎么骂你的吗？”

en: All right, everything is already fine now, isn't it? Don't be so fierce!
u.src: “好了，不是已经没事了嘛！不要那么凶！”

en: Mother closed her eyes in annoyance.
u.src: 母亲很烦的闭上眼睛。

en: But my elder brother would not listen to Mother’s advice at all, and went on scolding me: “You are already fifteen. How can you still be so childish?
u.src: 不过，哥哥根本听不进母亲的劝告，继续骂道：“已经十五岁了，怎么还是这么不懂事呢？

en: They are only hina dolls. What is there to be so reluctant to part with?”
u.src: 只不过是雏人偶罢了，有什么好舍不得的呢？”

en: Mind your own business, that is not your doll!
u.src: “多管闲事，那又不是你的雏人偶！”

en: I, too, refused to admit defeat and talked back.
u.src: 我也不甘认输的反驳。

en: At first, it was just like before, with each of us answering the other back in an argument,
u.src: 起初还跟刚才一样，你一言我一语的争吵，

en: but then, to my surprise, my older brother grabbed the hair at the back of my neck
u.src: 没想到后来哥哥竟然抓着我脖子后面的头发

en: knocked me down to the ground, and went on scolding me: "You wild girl!"
u.src: 把我打倒在地，继续骂道：“野丫头！”

en: If Mother had not stopped him in time, I would surely have been hit by him two or three more times.
u.src: 如果不是母亲及时阻止，我肯定还要挨他两三下打吧。

en: Mother half raised her head from the pillow and said, half scolding, "What has Otsuru done wrong? Why treat her like this?"
u.src: 母亲从枕头上半抬起头，半骂道：“阿鹤没什么错，为什么要这么对待她？”

en: No matter what we say to her, she just won't listen.
u.src: “怎么跟她说，她都不听。”

ja: だけではないでしょう、
en: The person you hate isn't just Otsuru, is it? You... you...
u.src: “你憎恨的人不只是阿鹤一个人吧，你……你……”

en: Her mother had tears in her eyes and looked deeply distressed, several times seeming about to speak but stopping herself.
u.src: 母亲泪盈于眶，看起来很是懊恼，几次欲言又止。

en: The person you hate is me, isn't it?
u.src: “你憎恨的人是我吧？
对吗？

en: Otherwise, why would you insist on selling the hina dolls now, knowing full well that I am ill...
u.src: 不然为什么明知我在病中，偏要这个时候卖掉雏人偶……

en: You want to sell the hina dolls, and you torment O-Tsuru like this as well.
u.src: 要卖掉雏人偶，还如此欺负阿鹤。

ja: んでいるからでないなら、
en: If it is not because you hate me, why would you do such a thing?
u.src: 如果不是因为憎恨我，为什么要这么做呢？
是吗？
你为什么憎恨我呢？”
“妈妈！”

en: My brother suddenly cried out, then stood beside Mother's bed and buried his face in the crook of both arms.
u.src: 哥哥突然喊了一声，就站在母亲床边，把脸埋在双肘里面。

en: That brother, who did not cry even when our parents later died, who spent years rushing about for politics until he was finally sent to a mental hospital, and who had never shown fear to anyone,
u.src: 后来父母去世都没哭过的哥哥——常年为了政治奔波，直至最后被送进疯人院，从未对人展示过胆怯——这样的哥哥，

en: that brother, at this very moment, unexpectedly began to sob.
u.src: 此时此刻竟然啜泣起来。

en: Even for Mother, whose emotions were somewhat stirred, this must have been completely unexpected.
u.src: 这对于情绪有点激动的母亲，也是十分意外的吧。

en: Mother let out a deep sigh, started to speak and stopped, then lay back on the pillow again...
u.src: 母亲深深的叹了一口气，欲言又止，重新躺会枕头上……

en: About an hour after this quarrel had ended.
u.src: 经过这场争执，约莫一个小时之后。

en: There was Tokuzo the fishmonger, who had not come to the shop in a long time.
u.src: 很久没来店铺的鱼贩德藏。

en: No, he is a fishmonger now.
u.src: 不，他如今是鱼贩了。

en: He had once been a fishmonger, but now he was a rickshaw man, a young fellow who often came in and out of the house.
u.src: 他过去曾是个鱼贩，如今是个人力车夫，是经常来家里走动的年轻人。

en: This Tokuzo had been the cause of many comic stories.
u.src: 这个德藏闹过很多笑话。

en: The one I remember most clearly among them was a joke about surnames.
u.src: 其中我记得比较清楚的是有关姓氏的笑话。

en: Tokuzo, too, only took a surname after the Meiji Restoration,
u.src: 德藏也是在明治维新之后才取的姓氏，

en: and at the time he must have thought that if he was going to take a surname,
u.src: 那时候他可能觉得既然要取个姓氏，

en: of course it ought to be a very grand one,
u.src: 当然要取个非常高端的，

en: and so he chose Tokugawa as his surname.
u.src: 于是他自取“德川”作为姓氏。

en: However, when he went to the government office to register it,
u.src: 不过，他去政务所登记的时候，

en: the clerk gave him a terrible scolding.
u.src: 被办事员骂的狗血淋头。
按照德藏自己的说法，

ja: ろうとするほどだった。
en: the clerk was so angry that it seemed as if he meant to drag him out and behead him.
u.src: 当时办事员愤怒的程度就跟要把他拖出去问斩一般。

en: Now, on that day, Tokuzo came pulling his own rickshaw, which was painted with peonies and Chinese lions,
u.src: 话说那天，德藏拉着自己的人力车——车上画着牡丹和唐朝狮子，

en: and arrived at the shop in a carefree, cheerful mood.
u.src: 轻松愉快的 来到店里。

en: I had assumed he must have come because something important had happened,
u.src: 本来以为他有什么大事才过来的，
没想到他说：

en: There are not many customers today,
u.src: “今天没什么客人，

en: so I thought I would take the young lady for a ride to Brick Shop Street near Tsuhara.
u.src: 所以想拉着小姐到津原附近的砖屋大街上去逛逛。”

en: “Ah He, would you like to go out for a little stroll?”
u.src: “阿鹤，想不想去去逛逛？”

en: My father stared sternly at me as I ran outside the shop to look at the rickshaws.
u.src: 父亲严肃的盯着跑到店外看人力车的我。

en: Children today probably would not find much to be happy about in riding a rickshaw.
u.src: 现在的孩子坐人力车估计没什么可开心的了。

en: But in those days we were as thrilled to ride in a rickshaw as if we were riding in an automobile.
u.src: 不过当时的我们对坐人力车就像坐汽车一样兴奋不已。

en: But I was ill just then, and after such a fierce quarrel had just taken place, I simply could not bring myself to say that I really wanted to go.
u.src: 但是，目前正在病中，刚才有发生了那样激烈的争吵，我实在说不出自己很想去的话。

en: Still looking deflated, I said in a low voice, "I want to go."
u.src: 我依旧一副泄了气的样子，低声说：“想去。”

en: Ask your mother what she thinks, and tell her that this is Tokuzo's kind gesture.
u.src: “你去问问妈妈的建议，告诉她这是德藏的一片好意。”

en: Mother, as I had hoped, granted my wish; she smiled with her eyes closed and said, "Very well."
u.src: 母亲果然满足了我的愿望，闭着眼睛笑了笑，说：“很好啊。”

en: At that moment, my spiteful elder brother happened to be out of the house, having gone to the Marusa antique shop.
u.src: 当时，坏心眼的哥哥刚好不在家，去丸佐古董店了。

en: In that instant, I seemed to forget all the unpleasantness I had just gone through and hurriedly climbed into the rickshaw.
u.src: 那一瞬间我好像忘了刚才经历的所有不愉快，赶紧坐上了人力车。

en: I spread the blanket over my knees, and with the rickshaw wheels rumbling, we set off.
u.src: 我把毯子盖在膝上，人力车的轮子发出“咕噜咕噜”的声音，出发了。

en: There is no need to say much about the scenery we passed then.
u.src: 当时路过的风景也无需多说。

en: But even now I still remember the grumbling Tokuzo muttered at the time.
u.src: 但是我到现在还记得当时德藏念叨的牢骚。

en: Tokuzo was pulling me, and just before we reached Brick House Street, we nearly collided head on with a carriage carrying a Western woman.
u.src: 德藏载着我，快到砖屋大街之前，险些迎面撞上一辆载着西洋女人的马车。

en: Although no accident happened, he still said in vexation:
u.src: 虽然没发生任何事故，但他仍然懊恼的说：
“这样可不行啊！

en: Miss, you are too light, and the rickshaw man's two legs cannot brake properly.
u.src: 小姐的体重太轻了，车夫的两条腿听刹不住。

en: Miss, the rickshaw man who has to carry you really has my pity!
u.src: 小姐，载着你的车夫很可怜呢！

en: Until you are twenty, please do not ride in a rickshaw again!
u.src: 二十岁以前就别再坐人力车啦！”

en: The rickshaw passed along Brickhouse Street and turned into the alley leading toward home.
u.src: 人力车从砖屋大街通过，转向回家方向的巷子。

en: Suddenly, on the road, we ran into my elder brother Eikichi.
u.src: 突然，路上碰见了哥哥英吉。

en: My brother was carrying an oil lamp in his hand, a lamp with a soot-blackened bamboo pattern on it, and was hurrying along.
u.src: 哥哥手上拎着一盏油灯——油灯上有煤熏成的竹子图案，正匆忙赶路。

en: As soon as he saw me, he raised the oil lamp to signal, Wait a moment.
u.src: 一看到我，便举起油灯示意“等一下”。

en: Tokuzo moved with great agility, turning the shafts as he brought the rickshaw to a stop beside my brother.
u.src: 德藏的动作很是灵敏，一边转动车辕，一边把车停在了哥哥身旁。

en: Thank you for your hard work, Ade. Where are you all going?
u.src: “辛苦你了，阿德，你们这是去哪里呢？”

en: Ha ha, I brought the young lady to Edo for an outing today.
u.src: “呵呵，今天带着小姐来江户游玩。”

en: My older brother gave a wry smile, walked over beside the rickshaw, and said to me, "
u.src: 哥哥面露苦笑，走到人力车旁边，对我说：“

en: A-Tsuru, please take the oil lamp home for me.
u.src: 阿鹤，你帮我把油灯带回家。

en: I still have to go to the kerosene shop once more."
u.src: 我还要再去趟煤油铺。”

en: I remembered that I had quarreled with him just now, so I said nothing and only reached out to take the oil lamp.
u.src: 我想起刚才跟他吵过架，所以一声不吭，只是伸手接过油灯。

en: My older brother turned to leave, but unexpectedly he suddenly turned back,
u.src: 哥哥转身就走，没想到突然有转回头，

en: put his hand on the rickshaw's fender, and said:
u.src: 把手放在人力车的挡泥板上，说：

en: "O-Tsuru, don't talk to Father about the dolls anymore."
u.src: “阿鹤，你别再跟爸爸说雏人偶的事情了。”

ja: をするつもりなのかと
en: I still said nothing, thinking to myself, after bullying me like that just now, what could he possibly want to do now?
u.src: 我依然一声不吭，心理暗想，刚才那么欺负我，现在难道又想做什么吗？

en: But my brother did not mind at all and went on saying, "
u.src: 但是，哥哥一点也不介意，继续说：“

ja: ったからだけじゃない。
en: The reason Father will not let you look at the hina dolls is not only that he has already taken a deposit from the buyer.
u.src: 爸爸之所以不让你看雏人偶，不仅仅是因为收下了人家的定金。

ja: えてやってくれないか。
en: He is also worried that the more he looks at them, the harder it will be to part with them, so please think about Father a little too, all right?
u.src: 也是担心越看越舍不得——你也要替爸爸考虑一下，行吗？

en: Do you understand? Do you understand?
u.src: 懂了吗？懂了吗？

en: Do not fuss again like you did just now, saying you want to see them one more time."
u.src: 不要跟刚才一样吵着要再看一眼了。”

en: I felt a tenderness in my brother's voice that I had never heard before.
u.src: 我感觉哥哥的声音里有一种前所未有的温柔。

en: But there was no one in the world more awkward and contrary than my brother.
u.src: 但是，世界上没有比哥哥更别扭的人了。

en: Though he had just been speaking to me with emotion and tenderness, he suddenly returned to his usual coldness,
u.src: 刚刚还感性温柔的对我说话，忽然又恢复了平日的冷漠，

en: and threatened me, saying, "If you will not behave and listen to me, then do as you please.
u.src: 威胁说：“如果不乖一点听话的话，就随便你。

en: But you had better watch yourself, or I will make things very unpleasant for you."
u.src: 但是你给我小心点，不然我让你很难看。”

en: After his older brother finished speaking in a fierce tone,
he did not even say anything to Tokuzo,
and hurried off again to who knew where.
u.src: 哥哥凶狠的放完话，也没再跟德藏打招呼，又匆忙的不知道去哪了。
这是那天晚上的事情。

en: At the time, the four of us in the family were gathered around the dining table in the storehouse, eating supper.
u.src: 当时，我们一家四口围在仓库的饭桌旁吃晚饭。

en: In truth, Mother was still lying in bed and had only raised her head slightly, so she could hardly be said to be gathered around the table.
u.src: 其实，母亲还躺在床上，只是微微扬起头来而已，算不得围在饭桌旁。

en: But supper that night was brighter than it had ever been before.
u.src: 但是，那天晚上的晚饭比过去任何时候都明朗。

en: That was because a shining new oil lamp had replaced the dim old endless lamp.
u.src: 因为闪亮的新油灯代替了昏暗的老式无尽灯。

en: Between bites, my elder brother and I could not help glancing again and again at the oil lamp.
u.src: 哥哥和我在吃饭的间隙，总是不由的时不时看向油灯。

en: Through the glass, pot-shaped shade, we could clearly see the kerosene inside,
u.src: 透过玻璃壶形状的灯罩，能够清楚的看见里面的煤油，

en: and the flame, protected by the shade, did not flicker wildly. What a beautiful, marvelous oil lamp it was!
u.src: 火焰被灯罩保护着不至于胡乱晃动——真是美丽神奇的油灯啊！

en: The room is so bright, just like daytime.
u.src: “屋里真明亮，就像白天一样。”

en: Father looked at Mother and said with complete satisfaction.
u.src: 父亲看着母亲，心满意足的说道。

en: "It really is dazzlingly bright!" her mother said uneasily.
u.src: “真是亮的炫人眼目呢！”母亲不安的说道。

en: That is because we had grown used to the mujinto lamp.
u.src: “那是因为用习惯了无尽灯的缘故。

en: But once you have used an oil lamp, you no longer want to go back to using the mujinto lamp.
u.src: 但是，只要用过油灯，就在也不想回去使用无尽灯了。”

en: All new things seem dazzling to people at first!
u.src: “所有新鲜事物，起初的时候都会让人觉得炫目啊！

en: In short, whether it is oil lamps or Western knowledge and learning...
u.src: 总而言之，不管是油灯，还是西方的知识学问……”

en: My elder brother said it with more enthusiasm than anyone else.
u.src: 哥哥比任何人都充满劲头的说道。

en: Once people get used to it, it will be exactly the same as before.
u.src: “等到习惯了就跟以前完全一样了。

en: I believe that before long everyone will enter an age when they think oil lamps are too dim.
u.src: 我相信很快大家就会进入认为油灯太暗的时代。”

ja: にそうなのかもしれないね
en: Maybe that really is how it is... Otsuru, how is the rice soup you are making for Mother coming along?
u.src: “可能真的就是这样吧……阿鹤，帮妈妈熬的米汤如何了？”

en: Mom said she felt too bloated tonight to eat.
u.src: “妈妈说她觉得今晚肚子太胀了，吃不下。”

en: I absentmindedly relayed what my mother had said earlier.
u.src: 我心不在焉的传达妈妈之前讲的话。

en: How can that be all right?
u.src: “那怎么行呢？

en: Do you not want to eat even a little?
u.src: 一点也不想吃吗？”

en: Pressed by her husband with such questions, the mother let out a long sigh helplessly.
u.src: 母亲被父亲如此追问，无奈的长叹了一口气。

en: Yes, somehow the smell of kerosene feels a little... I suppose that means I really am old-fashioned.
u.src: “是啊，总觉得煤油的气味有些……这说明我到底是个守旧的人呢。”

en: After that, everyone spoke less and less, and they simply kept moving their chopsticks and eating.
u.src: 之后大家的话越来越少了，都只一个劲的动筷子吃饭罢了。

en: But Mother suddenly seemed to remember something and kept praising how bright the oil lamp was; even the sore on her lip seemed to be smiling.
u.src: 但是母亲却突然像想起什么一样，不住地夸奖油灯的明亮，就连嘴唇上的肿疮都好像挂着微笑。

en: That night, everyone turned out the lights and went to bed only after eleven o'clock.
u.src: 那天晚上，大家都是过了十一点才熄灯休息。

en: But after I closed my eyes, I could not fall asleep no matter what.
u.src: 但是，我闭上眼睛之后，无论如何都睡不着。

en: My elder brother had already warned me several times not to bring up the dolls, and I had given up asking to see them once more.
u.src: 哥哥已经数次警告我不准我提起雏人偶的事情了，我对再看一眼雏人偶的要求也已经死心了。

en: Even so, my desire to see the dolls once more had not changed in the slightest.
u.src: 但是，我想再看一眼雏人偶的想法也丝毫没有改变。

en: Tomorrow the dolls would be sent away to some far-off household, and whenever I thought of it my tears would not stop flowing.
u.src: 明天，雏人偶就要被送到遥远的别人家了——只要想到这件事，我的眼泪就止不住的流下来。

en: Perhaps I should wait until everyone was asleep, secretly take them out myself, and have one more look.
u.src: 要不然等大家都睡着了，我自己偷偷拿出来看一眼。

en: That thought had crossed my mind.
u.src: ——我曾经有过这样的念头。

en: Or perhaps I could take out one of the dolls and secretly hide it away.
u.src: 或者把某一个雏人偶拿出来，偷偷藏起来。
——我也有过这种念头。

en: But whichever I did, if I were discovered, the mere thought of that possibility made me shudder uncontrollably.
u.src: 但是不管是哪一样，一旦被发现——想到这个可能，我就忍不住一阵战栗。

en: To be honest, never in my life had my mind been so filled with strange ideas as it was that night.
u.src: 老实说，我这一辈子从未像那一晚，脑子里想的都是奇奇怪怪的想法。

en: For example, I wished a great fire might break out that very night.
u.src: 譬如：倘若今晚来一场大火就好了。

en: Before the dolls were handed over, the fire would burn them all to ashes.
u.src: 在没有把雏人偶交出去之前，就把它们都烧光了。

en: Or the American who lived in Yokohama and the owner of the Marusa shop might both come down with cholera.
u.src: 或者那个住在横滨的美国人和丸佐店的老板都得了霍乱。

en: If that happened, the dolls would not have to be sent away and would remain safely in my house.
u.src: 要是这样的话，雏人偶就不用被送走了，还会好好地留在我家里。

en: Those were the absurd thoughts that filled my mind.
u.src: ——我想的都是这些荒谬的想法。

en: But after all, I was still a child then, and in less than an hour I drifted drowsily off to sleep.
u.src: 但是，无论如何当时我还是一个孩子，约莫不到一个小时，我就迷迷糊糊的睡着了。

en: After I do not know how long, I suddenly woke up,
u.src: 不知道过了多长时间，我猛然醒了过来，

en: It seemed that someone had lit a dim lantern in the storeroom, and there was a faint sound of movement.
u.src: 仓库里好像有人点上了昏暗的灯笼，有些许动静。
有老鼠？
还是有小偷？
还是天已经亮了？

en: I did not know which it was, so I timidly opened my eyes and looked.
u.src: ——我不知道到底是那种状况，胆怯的睁开眼看了看。

en: It was Father, wearing his nightclothes and sitting sideways beside my bed.
u.src: 原来是父亲穿着睡衣，侧身坐在我床边。
爸爸！

en: But it was not only Father who surprised me,
u.src: 但是让我吃惊的不仅仅是父亲，

en: for in front of him were my hina dolls,
u.src: 而且父亲面前摆放着我的雏人偶——

en: the hina dolls I had not seen again since the Girls' Day festival on March third.
u.src: 从三月三女儿节一来，再也没见过的雏人偶。

en: I wondered to myself, could I be dreaming?
u.src: 我心想难道我是在做梦嘛！

en: I held my breath and stared intently at the unbelievable scene before my eyes.
u.src: 我凝神屏气的看着眼前难以置信的景象。

en: In the dim light spilling from the swaying lantern, the emperor held an ivory ritual baton,
u.src: 在摇晃的灯笼透出的昏暗灯光下，手持象牙笏的天皇，

en: the empress wore a jeweled crown, with an orange tree on the right and a cherry tree on the left,
u.src: 头戴璎珞皇冠的皇后，右边的橘子树，左边的樱花树，

en: a lady-in-waiting held up a long-handled parasol, and a court lady held a wine cup level with her brows,
u.src: 举着长柄阳伞的侍女，手持齐眉酒杯的宫女，

en: there were tiny maki-e mirror stands and cabinets, shell-made folding screens, and eating bowls,
u.src: 小小的莳绘镜台和柜子，贝壳材质的屏风，食碗，

en: paper lanterns, colored balls, and even my father's profile...
u.src: 纸灯笼、彩色的球，以及父亲的侧脸……
难道我是在做梦吗？

en: Ah, I already said that just now.
u.src: 啊，这句话我刚才已经说过了。

en: But was it really only a doll I had dreamed of that night?
u.src: 但是，那天晚上真的只是梦见的雏人偶吗？

en: Could it have been because I had longed so much to see the dolls that I had such a hallucination?
u.src: 难道是因为自己心心念念想看雏人偶，所以才会有这种幻觉吗？

en: Even today, I still do not know whether that night was a dream or reality.
u.src: 即便到了今天，我也不知道那晚究竟是梦境，还是真实的。

en: But I truly saw my father at midnight, alone and gazing at those hina dolls.
u.src: 但是，我确实在半夜看见父亲，一个人凝视着那些雏人偶。

en: Even if it was only a dream, I have no regrets.
u.src: 即便那只是一场梦，我也心无遗憾。

en: In short, the father I saw before me, like me, was deeply reluctant to part with the hina dolls...
u.src: 总而言之，我眼前的看到的父亲和我一样，都对雏人偶万分不舍……

en: Even so, my father was still a stern father.
u.src: 尽管如此，父亲仍然是个严肃的父亲。

en: It has already been several years since I wrote Hina Dolls.
u.src: 我写《雏人偶》已经是几年前的事情了。

en: The reason I have only now finished it is not simply because of Mr. Enda's urging,
u.src: 直到现在才写完并不仅仅是因为淹田氏的劝说，

en: but rather because about four or five days ago, in the sitting room of a certain Englishman's house in Yokohama,
u.src: 更是因为约莫四五天前，我在住在横滨的某一个英国人家的客厅里，

en: I saw a red-haired little girl playing with the head of an old hina doll as a toy.
u.src: 看到一个红发女童将一个陈旧的雏人偶的头当做玩具玩。

en: The hina doll in this story too, by now perhaps along with lead soldiers, rubber toys, and the like,
u.src: 这个故事里的雏人偶，现在可能也和铅制的士兵、橡胶的玩具等等，

en: has probably been packed away in a toy box and is suffering a similar misfortune.
u.src: 一起被装进玩具箱里，遭受相似的不幸吧。
